Standard group-embedding workflow: dimensionality, final fit, choice-model refit

run_group_embedding_workflow.Rd

Chains together the three steps of this package's standard recipe for producing a production group embedding:

  1. Dimensionality. estimate_dimensionality searches over dims under the crowd-kernel choice model (\(\alpha = 1\)), selecting best_d via its one-standard-error rule.

  2. Final fit. run_group_embedding_from_list is called n_restarts_final times at best_d, each from an independent random initialization, keeping whichever restart achieves the lowest test loss. This is a dedicated refit, not a reuse of one of the embeddings fitted during step 1 – see the Why a dedicated final fit section below.

  3. Choice-model refit. estimate_group_alpha takes the winning final fit as a warm start and coordinate-ascends between re-estimating the Student-t/crowd-kernel shape \(\alpha\) and refitting the embedding under it, using held-out sampleAlg == "validation" trials to profile \(\alpha\).

Usage

run_group_embedding_workflow(
  triplet_list,
  dims = 1:8,
  n_restarts_dim = 10L,
  n_restarts_final = 5L,
  internal_test_frac = 0.1,
  max_epochs = 50000L,
  tolerance = 1e-04,
  tol_window = 10000L,
  device = NULL,
  seed = 1L,
  geometry = c("euclidean", "sphere"),
  radius = 1,
  norm_penalty = 0,
  best_d_norm_penalty = NULL,
  refit_alpha = TRUE,
  max_outer = 15L,
  tol_log_alpha = 0.05,
  alpha_grid = 10^seq(log10(2e-04), log10(2e+06), length.out = 140),
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

triplet_list

A named list of data frames, one per participant, as returned by get.combined. Must contain a usable sampleSet column (see assign_sample_sets) and, if refit_alpha = TRUE, genuine sampleAlg == "validation" trials (see estimate_group_alpha).

dims

Integer vector of dimensionalities to evaluate in step 1. Default 1:8.

n_restarts_dim

Random restarts per dimension in step 1, forwarded to estimate_dimensionality's n_restarts. Default 10L.

n_restarts_final

Independent random restarts for the dedicated final fit in step 2; the restart with the lowest test loss is kept. Default 5L. Each restart uses seed seed + (r - 1) * 1000, the same restart-seed formula used throughout this package's Condor workflows.

internal_test_frac, max_epochs, tolerance, tol_window, device, norm_penalty

Forwarded to estimate_dimensionality (step 1) and run_group_embedding_from_list (step 2); max_epochs, tolerance, tol_window, device, and norm_penalty are also forwarded to estimate_group_alpha (step 3). internal_test_frac is only used by step 1 (see that function's own documentation).

seed

Base integer seed. Step 1 receives it directly; step 2's restarts derive seed + (r - 1) * 1000 from it; step 3 receives it directly as its own seed.

geometry

Either "euclidean" (default) or "sphere", forwarded to steps 1 and 2. estimate_group_alpha (step 3) does not currently support geometry = "sphere"; this function errors clearly if geometry = "sphere" and refit_alpha = TRUE rather than silently refitting a Euclidean embedding when a spherical one was requested. Set refit_alpha = FALSE to use spherical geometry for steps 1-2 alone.

radius

Sphere radius when geometry = "sphere". Default 1.

best_d_norm_penalty

Forwarded to estimate_dimensionality. Default NULL (equal to norm_penalty).

refit_alpha

Logical; if TRUE (default), run step 3. Set to FALSE to stop after the final fit (step 2) – e.g. when triplet_list has no sampleAlg == "validation" trials yet.

max_outer, tol_log_alpha, alpha_grid

Forwarded to estimate_group_alpha (step 3); ignored if refit_alpha = FALSE.

verbose

Logical; print a progress line at the start of each step and for each final-fit restart. Default TRUE. Forwarded to estimate_dimensionality and estimate_group_alpha.

Value

A named list with four elements:

dimensionality

The full return value of estimate_dimensionality (step 1): results and summary.

best_d

The selected dimensionality (smallest d with summary$best_d == TRUE).

final_fit

The winning restart's return value from run_group_embedding_from_list (step 2): embedding, loss, history – the crowd-kernel (\(\alpha = 1\)) production embedding at best_d.

refit

NULL if refit_alpha = FALSE; otherwise the return value of estimate_group_alpha (step 3): embedding (the refit geometry), alpha, log_alpha, ci, history.

Why a dedicated final fit

Steps 1 and 3 both already exist as standalone functions; what this wrapper adds is the final-fit step in between, plus the glue to chain all three. Reusing the single best-loss embedding that happened to come out of step 1's (dimension, restart) grid would tie the production embedding to whatever restart budget that grid spent per dimension – necessarily small, since it is multiplied across every dimension in dims. A dedicated final-fit step is a one-time cost (not multiplied by a dimension grid), so it is the cheapest place in the whole workflow to spend extra restart budget on the one embedding that is actually used downstream. This mirrors inst/condor/condor_workflow.py's existing three-stage Condor architecture (dimensionality search, learning curve, final embedding fit), which already treats the final fit as a separate stage rather than a reuse of a dimensionality-search artifact; the Condor workflow's own final stage (condor_fit.R, stage == "final") gained the same n_restarts-and-keep-lowest-loss logic for the same reason.

Picking the lowest test loss among n_restarts_final restarts is a mild "best of k" selection, so that restart's own test loss is a slightly optimistic estimate of its true generalization loss – the same kind of optimism inherent in selecting best_d itself. This is a standard, usually small effect with k in the single digits, not something this function tries to correct for.

Dimension estimation and the test set

estimate_dimensionality's internal sampleSet == "test" pool is never touched during dimensionality search (see that function's own Internal test set and restart variability section) – it is reserved for this function's step 2, exactly as run_group_embedding_from_list uses it. That means the same sampleSet train/test split, assigned once upstream (e.g. via assign_sample_sets), is reused consistently across all three steps of this workflow – the dimensionality search is not re-randomizing or resampling that top-level split per restart; the resampling it does do (see estimate_dimensionality's internal_test_frac) happens entirely within the "train" pool, matched across every dimension for a given restart so dimension comparisons stay apples-to-apples.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
out <- run_group_embedding_workflow(
  triplet_list     = icon_triplets,
  dims             = 1:6,
  n_restarts_dim   = 5L,
  n_restarts_final = 5L
)
out$best_d
out$final_fit$embedding       # crowd-kernel (alpha = 1) production embedding
out$refit$embedding           # choice-model-refit embedding
out$refit$alpha               # estimated choice-model shape parameter

# Stop after the final fit (e.g. no validation trials available yet)
out2 <- run_group_embedding_workflow(icon_triplets, refit_alpha = FALSE)
out2$refit  # NULL
} # }
